Classification guard: the mapping asserts the self-injury-to-wound-outcome association documented in the dermatitis-artefacta literature; individual claims require documented self-inflicted lesions preceding documented scarring and exclusion of organic dermatologic disease and independent scar etiologies.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 32 (2026-09-23): one bounded scars association authored from the dermatitis-artefacta outcome literature - the Alcolado 1993 report documents four decades of persistent excoriation of a scar site producing an enlarged disfiguring lesion and death from Marjolin-type malignant transformation, the Rodríguez Pichardo 2013 review of 201 patients documents chronic self-inflicted lesions including ulcers, and the Choudhary 2009 case documents keloids and foreign-body granuloma from self-inflicted acupuncture-ideation injury; the self-injury-to-wound-repair sequence is the accepted biology but individual scar burden is self-injury pattern dependent.

Duplicate-scope note: the excoriation-disorder identity carries its own scars edge scoped to compulsive picking behavior, so this factitious-disorder edge is the sole conscious-self-injury-to-scar pathway; dermatitis artefacta is the cutaneous presentation of factitious disorder, keeping the two behavioral identities on their own mechanisms.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Rodríguez Pichardo 2013 review of 201 patients with dermatitis artefacta (the cutaneous presentation of factitious disorder) documents chronic self-inflicted lesions including ulcers at accessible sites, the Alcolado 1993 case documents four decades of persistent self-excoriation of a scar site with malignant transformation and death from metastatic squamous carcinoma, and the Choudhary 2009 case documents keloids and foreign-body granuloma produced by deliberate self-inflicted injury; the literature connects conscious self-injury to wound outcomes but does not quantify an individual scarring nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The mapping does not assert that every scar in a person with factitious disorder was self-inflicted: organic dermatologic disease, surgical scars, and self-harm from other psychiatric conditions independently scar; individual claims require documented self-inflicted lesions preceding documented scars, anatomic distribution over accessible skin that does not match organic disease patterns, and exclusion of organic scarring disease.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized deliberate-self-injury wound-repair pathway: repeated deliberate trauma to accessible skin (excoriation, manipulation, or introduction of foreign material) breaches the epidermis and dermis; each wound triggers the normal repair sequence - inflammation, granulation, and collagen deposition - and chronic unhealed lesions, repeated re-injury of the same sites, and foreign-body reaction produce hypertrophic scarring, keloids, and chronic ulcers that are clinically documented in the dermatitis-artefacta series and case reports; individual scar burden tracks self-injury pattern, chronicity, and secondarily infected lesions rather than the disorder label itself.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: the 201-patient series and case reports document chronic self-inflicted lesions and their outcomes, but scarring also follows organic dermatologic disease, surgery, trauma, and self-harm from other psychiatric conditions, diagnosis of dermatitis artefacta is by exclusion, and no cohort quantifies scar risk attributable to the factitious behavior independent of these confounders; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented self-inflicted lesions with anatomic distribution over accessible skin; dermatologic examination documenting scars and their chronology relative to self-injury episodes; exclusion of organic dermatologic disease by biopsy or clinical characterization; assessment of keloidal predisposition and foreign-body reaction; psychiatric assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Organic dermatologic disease independently causing scarring
Surgical, traumatic, or burn scars unrelated to self-injury
Deliberate self-harm from depressive or other psychiatric disease (distinct mechanism)
Keloidal predisposition (keloid disorder) with incidental trauma

evidenceGaps: Documented self-inflicted lesions with anatomic distribution over accessible skin; dermatologic examination documenting scars and their chronology relative to self-injury episodes; exclusion of organic dermatologic disease by biopsy or clinical characterization; assessment of keloidal predisposition and foreign-body reaction; psychiatric assessment of the individual relationship
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: case reports and the 201-patient review document chronic self-inflicted ulcers and scar outcomes, but no condition-specific cohort establishes an individual causal nexus, so the mapping asserts the association and requires individual psychiatric and dermatologic documentation.
